source.description: A reviewed six-panel raster correction sheet supplies three distinct replacement construction frames; the approved ink, color, and finished masters remain unchanged.
source.notes: Step 1 must stay sparse, Step 2 must add the readable submarine silhouette, and Step 3 must install every window and hardware detail before the preserved black-marker frame. Keep one face-free submarine, one capsule hull, one tower, one bent periscope, exactly three portholes, two tail fins, one three-blade propeller, one lower side fin, exactly six rivets, three bubbles, and one broken water shadow stable.

process_strategy: Begin with only a pale dive axis, capsule envelope, attachment axes, feature centers, and shadow footprint; add the full hull, tower, bent periscope, fins, propeller gestures, and bubble guides in Step 2; install every porthole, rivet, seam, refined blade, refined bubble, and shadow contour in Step 3; then preserve the approved ink, color, and finish frames unchanged.

final_elements.name: sparse dive scaffold and reserved feature positions
final_elements.description: Pale construction fixes one tilted centerline, a loose capsule envelope, a small tower box, tail and fin axes, a propeller hub axis, three porthole centers, three bubble centers, and a broken shadow footprint without drawing finished contours.

final_elements.description: One readable submarine with a rounded capsule hull, small tower, persistent bent periscope, tapered tail housing, two tail fins, one lower side fin, a propeller hub with three light blade gestures, and exactly three light bubble circles.

final_elements.name: three portholes seam six rivets and refined hardware
final_elements.description: Exactly three round portholes, one hull seam, exactly six rivets, three refined propeller blades, three refined bubbles in three sizes, and the complete broken shadow outline.

final_elements.name: thick black felt-tip outline and broken water shadow
final_elements.description: Handmade black marker reinforces every established contour while one broken oval water shadow grounds the submarine.

final_elements.name: mustard navy rust and seafoam marker fills
final_elements.description: A limited vintage-marine palette fills the established hull, windows, fins, bubbles, and shadow with visible marker streaks and highlight gaps.

rejection_checks: Keep the same face-free submarine, upward tilt, crop, scale, hull proportions, tower, fins, propeller, and bubble placement in all six panels.

Step 1 must remain a sparse primitive scaffold, Step 2 must visibly add the complete silhouette and attachments, and Step 3 must visibly add the windows and hardware; reject any repair where these frames read as the same drawing with darker lines.
The bent periscope introduced with the Step 2 silhouette must remain visible in every later panel; it may never disappear and return.
Exactly three portholes, six rivets, three bubbles, two tail fins, one three-blade propeller, and one lower side fin must appear before bold ink or color and persist.
Do not introduce a porthole, rivet, bubble, seam, fin, propeller blade, periscope bend, shadow shape, or color area in the final panel.
Do not add eyes, mouth, passenger, fish, seabed, coral, text, label, arrow, number, signature, watermark, sticker border, or badge frame.
The finish must retain visible felt-tip streaks and imperfect handmade edges rather than vector-clean icon art or polished poster rendering.
